written: 2026-09-22, before the lookup existed (WG.0 promise 3): the coordinates and expectations come from references named beside each, not from the atlas. Elevation ranges allow for a 9 km cell's mean; a climate expectation of 'present' at sea follows CHELSA V2.1's documented global coverage, observed once at (0, -150) on 2026-09-22 before these probes were run.

probes.name: bherwerre
probes.source: the region's own centre (Region.Bherwerre); Parks Australia: sedimentary bedrock, sand; the Bureau's Point Perpendicular record: about 1240 mm a year

probes.name: simpson-desert
probes.source: Munga-Thirri-Simpson Desert (the design's second walkthrough): parallel dunes of sand, 100 to 250 mm of rain a year, RESOLVE's Simpson desert, Lake Eyre some 250 km south-west

probes.name: sagarmatha
probes.source: Sagarmatha / the upper Dudh Kosi (the design's third walkthrough): the valley floors near 3,500 to 4,500 m with peaks over 6,000 m in a 9 km cell, RESOLVE's Eastern Himalayan alpine shrub and meadows, the Bay of Bengal some 600 km off

probes.name: antimeridian-east
probes.source: Taveuni, Fiji, a volcanic island rising to 1,241 m just west of the line; RESOLVE's Fiji tropical moist forests; among the wettest islands of the Pacific

probes.name: antimeridian-west
probes.source: the same coast of Taveuni a few kilometres east of the line, where the longitude is written as -179.95: the lookup must answer on both sides

probes.name: north-pole
probes.source: the Arctic Ocean, some 4,000 m deep at the pole, ice over sea: no land, no ecoregion, no rock class, CHELSA's grid ends at 84N, the nearest coast Greenland's about 700 km off

probes.name: south-pole
probes.source: the polar plateau of Antarctica, about 2,835 m of ice at the pole; CHELSA covers it; RESOLVE's Antarctic coverage is uncertain, so the ecoregion is not pinned; the nearest coast about 1,300 km

probes.name: open-ocean
probes.source: the South Pacific between Easter Island and Chile, abyssal plain some 3,000 to 4,500 m deep, no land within 1,500 km

revised: 2026-09-22, after the first run (Artefacts/atlas/probes-20260922T081153Z.json): seven of sixty-seven checks failed and each is revised here in the open, with what was first pinned and why it was wrong. Three were the references' errors: the Simpson Desert has salt lakes within 25 km of the probe (Natural Earth carries them); Easter Island lies about 1,100 km from the open-ocean probe, not over 1,500; and (-16.8, 179.9) is in the Somosomo Strait off Taveuni, a sea cell, which the coast at 9 km and the island answered across the line both say. Four are the sources' and the tool's limits, recorded in DEBTS: GLiM's half-degree grid leaves coastal cells empty (Bherwerre's rock reads none); the chamfer distances neither wrap at the date line (the nearest lake from -179.95 is measured the long way round) nor fill the last rows at the poles (the south pole's coast reads 550 km).
